concept.name: Balanced profile
concept.definition: A Market Profile structure in which the session's TPOs cluster in an overlapping, roughly bell-shaped distribution around a central value: buyers and sellers found relative agreement, and price rotated back and forth within a range. Consecutive days with overlapping ranges and value areas define a multi-day balance or bracket.
concept.intuition: A balanced profile is a market at rest: neither side had the conviction to reprice, so trade piled up around a fair central price.
concept.mechanics: Identified by a fat, symmetrical distribution (the classical D shape), TPOs concentrated around the POC, and range extensions absent or minor; balance is broken when new information drives acceptance outside the established range.
concept.failure_modes: Balance is always defined retrospectively and can persist far longer than expected or break the moment it is labeled; trading the range edges mechanically fails badly on the day balance finally resolves.
concept.misconceptions: Balance does not mean the market 'must' break out soon, nor that range-fading is a positive-expectancy strategy by default — it is a description of the current auction state, not a forecast.
concept.example: For four sessions ES trades between 4,500 and 4,540 with overlapping value areas; the composite profile shows one fat distribution, and traders treat the range edges as references until acceptance occurs outside them.
